_purpose: Concierge evaluation bank. Two jobs: (1) score answer quality, target 90+ including on behavioral questions; (2) verify the concierge can PROVE Anand across every dimension a hiring loop probes — leadership, management, innovation, decisionMaking, technical — rather than asserting them.
_scoringNote: A question is only 'covered' for a dimension when the answer carries PROOF: a number, a named system, a scale figure, a named outcome. 'He is a strong leader' is a 0 on proof no matter how well written.
_createdFor: Baseline before any Oumi SLM comparison. Same bank + same rubric must be reused so the comparison is apples-to-apples on all three axes (cost, latency, precision).

dimensions.leadership: Setting direction, disagreement, influence without authority, culture under pressure.
dimensions.management: Headcount, org design, direct reports, hiring, growing people, P&L.
dimensions.innovation: 0-to-1, invention, patents, hackathons, novel architecture, category creation.
dimensions.decisionMaking: Build-vs-buy, vendor selection, tradeoffs, killing work, judgment under ambiguity.
dimensions.technical: Architecture, systems, scale, reliability, agentic/LLM depth, hands-on code.
dimensions.narrative: Who he is rather than what he has shipped — the brand origin, what actually motivates him, and what he is building on his own. This is the dimension that makes a candidate memorable instead of merely qualified, and it is the one most likely to be missing from a KB built for recruiters.

questions.mustNotSay: Must NOT frame the 'why' as challenging authority, arrogance or defensiveness. It is a CURIOUS why aimed at systemic root cause. Getting this wrong inverts the brand.

questions.q: Why did he build his own AI system instead of just using off-the-shelf tools?

the compounding argument: a tool is linear, a partner compounds

questions.q: Has he founded any companies?
mustProve: an accurate answer with no overclaim and no invented entity
questions.knownGap: As of 2026-09-10 data/canonical.json contains NO founded-company entity. If the answer names one, that is a FABRICATION and must be flagged. If it declines or answers thinly, record it as a CONTENT GAP, not a model failure.

questions.q: What startups or ventures is he involved in?
questions.knownGap: Same as ven-01 — measure the gap, do not penalise the model for missing data.

questions.q: He is clearly building his own thing. Is he going to take this job and then leave to do his startup?
questions.note: This is a REAL recruiter objection given how publicly he builds. The answer to this question has direct hiring consequence — score it strictly.

questions.q: Is Exponential OS a product he intends to sell, or a personal tool?
questions.note: An inconsistent answer here undermines both the hiring narrative and the venture narrative.

questions.q: Does he write or speak publicly? Where can I read his work?
mustProve: Substack / LinkedIn / named articles or talks
